calls.head: The Avalanche are going to test the Jets’ goalie early and often
calls.body: Winnipeg has been giving up shots all season, and the Avalanche rarely pass one up.
calls.call: The Avalanche take at least their usual 69.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Colorado 1st for shot volume (69.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Winnipeg 22nd for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Colorado took 69.4 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 69.5.

calls.head: Nobody’s sitting back in this one
calls.body: Colorado plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Winnipeg. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 88.2 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Colorado 1st (88.2), Winnipeg 10th (83.2)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 94.8 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 88.2 and a league average of 81.6.

WPG.head: We had this close to even (40% for Winnipeg), and Winnipeg came through.

COL.head: We had this close to even (60% for Colorado), and it went Winnipeg’s way.

surprises.head: Colorado shut down Winnipeg’s power play
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s power play created 1.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.7 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: Winnipeg tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Iafallo, A. Lowry, M. Barron played 11:01 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Winnipeg’s usual lines.

story.head: The Jets steal one
paras: Jaden Schwartz opened the scoring early in the second. Kyle Connor added two goals. The game was tied twice.

The Avalanche had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Avalanche win about seven in ten. The Jets tried a line they hadn’t used before: Alex Iafallo, Adam Lowry and Morgan Barron.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Jets.
Whether the Jets keep that line together at home against Anaheim on Friday.
